A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SelfReflect research despite the changed title and presentation. All supplied pages, including v2 Appendices A–I and v3 Appendices A–M, are readable and support matching text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original summary-quality experiments, MMLU validation, a human preference study, and evaluations of summary-generation methods, with further empirical analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and adds broader metric validation, an ablation, and fine-tuning results in Appendix M.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix M add LoRA-based SFT, DPO, and combined training as summary-generation procedures, using sample-and-summarize targets and greedy negative examples. The central SelfReflect masked-word/Wasserstein metric, judge choice, temperature scaling, and existing prompted generation procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The dataset inventory remains Natural Questions, TriviaQA, SimpleQA, and MMLU. However, Study 1 extends controlled summary-quality validation from Natural Questions to TriviaQA and SimpleQA. The new fine-tuning study also adds cross-dataset transfer scenarios between Natural Questions and TriviaQA.

E2.justification: v3 adds SR-logl as a comparator in automated summary discrimination and MMLU validation (Tables 1–2 and 9–10). Existing comparison metrics remain, and SR-logl is not added to the retained human-study comparisons. Table 5's Basic-to-Reasoning header change denotes the existing procedure.

E3.justification: Study 2 expands from 1,000 Gemma-generated MMLU distributions to a reported 2×1,000 distributions, adding Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct. The new fine-tuning evaluation introduces 10,000-example training sets, held-out and cross-dataset evaluation, and experiments across 5–20 epochs, learning rates, and DPO settings. Existing summary-generation and SelfReflect estimation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The new SR-logl ablation tests whether comparing complete prediction vectors helps beyond comparing masked-word log probabilities. Appendix M adds a substantial training-generalization and sensitivity study across SFT/DPO configurations, epochs, learning rates, and beta values. Existing convergence, judge-choice, word-level examples, and CoT certainty analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for metric validation and human agreement, and specify 100 bootstrap samples for the user study. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures. Changed interval values and additional rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds multi-dataset discrimination results, second-generator MMLU results, SR-logl scores, and Table 16's fine-tuning outcomes. Tables 1–2 therefore reflect expanded settings, rather than directly comparable performance changes. Corresponding reported values also change: Natural Questions good-versus-almost-good accuracy is 94.20% in v2 Table 1 and 98.74% in v3 Table 9. Table 4 corrects Qwen 2.5 32B's N=20 relative difference from −0 to −5 while retaining the absolute score of 91.

T1.justification: The ideal-summary definition, predictive-sufficiency equivalences, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged. v3's boxed Definition 3.2 reproduces v2 Equation (4); equation renumbering and theorem formatting do not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 says models struggle and single-decoding methods do not consistently outperform Greedy. v3's abstract and introduction assert incapability across the board, explicitly extending the negative claim to SFT/DPO. The introduction makes this broader negative finding an explicit second contribution alongside the metric.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the fine-tuning results as memorizing individual summaries rather than learning general access to internal distributions. It also interprets the unchanged Figure 4 as showing near independence between CoT certainty and distributional certainty. Existing limitations concerning interpretability, summary length, and subjective faithfulness are retained in Appendix B.

D1.justification: v3 discloses LoRA use, training-example construction, epoch counts, learning rates, and selected DPO beta values for the new study. It removes v2's explicit vLLM parallelization and prefix-caching disclosure, without establishing a backend change. The code URL and existing implementation and prompt details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kadavath et al. (2022) for P(True) and Wei et al. (2024) for SimpleQA, and removes the Kwon et al. (2023) vLLM reference. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning relative to uncertainty quantification and summarization research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, Study 1 discussion, and Section 5 narrative. Section 5 is reorganized into setup, results, and CoT analysis; Discussion becomes Outlook, and limitations move to Appendix B. It also adds an appendix contents page and numbered prompts, changes the title, and adds Seong Joon Oh as an author.

P2.justification: v3 introduces a document-wide redesign with a branded title panel, wider text area, changed typography, colored cross-references, and shaded definition/theorem boxes. Existing displays are resized or relocated, Tables 1–2 gain SR-logl rows, and Tables 9, 10, and 16 are added. All 17 existing figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Broader validation, SR-logl, and training-transfer tests add useful evidence. However, v2's qualified failure-to-consistently-beat-Greedy conclusion becomes categorical despite retained numerical counterexamples in Table 4. Reporting also becomes inconsistent: v3 Table 2 gives Embedding's per-question correlation as −0.24, whereas Table 10 reports 0.29 and 0.02 for its two models, without reconciliation. The added evidence and unresolved reporting and claim-calibration problems leave the net quality change uncertain.
